inputs.share_count_basis: Shares eligible for profit distribution per FY2025 AR (26-Mar-2026 board resolution): 8,712.4m total A+H share capital less 50.25m treasury shares = 8,662.1m. Restricted-A-share scheme dilution is <0.1% and ignored. Held FLAT: SBC (0.03-0.1% of revenue) is expensed in the flows, buybacks (RMB761.5m FY2025) are the mechanism that keeps the count flat.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Metrics.csv StockBasedComp (restricted A-share incentive scheme expense, RMB66.5m). No net-share-settlement tax line exists for A-share restricted stock; immaterial.
inputs.fx_note: CNY->HKD 1.1724 (Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-16T22:01Z). Parity check against the A-share line: the 2026-10-16 H-share close converted at this rate sits 0.4% below the same day's 000338.SZ close in CNY (A-share price is in data_sources), which confirms rate, direction and quote basis. All flows and per-share values are computed in CNY and converted to HKD at this rate; the unsuffixed intrinsic values are HKD.
inputs.wacc_rationale: 9.0% blended, flows in CNY (~60% of revenue) and EUR (KION, ~40%). CNY leg: 10y CGB ~1.85% + beta 1.1 x China ERP 6.5% = ~9.0%. EUR leg: Bund ~2.7% + beta 1.2 x ERP 5.5% = ~9.3%. Debt is small against market cap and the KION finance-book debt is matched by lease assets, so WACC ~= cost of equity, rounded to 9.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality and electrification risk are charged in the bear flows and the 25% bear weight, not stacked as a premium (adaptation f).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: IFRS-16/CAS-21 lease cash (RMB1,793m FY2025, other financing cash note 68(6), incl. RMB258m lease interest) charged inside EBIT at 0.77% of revenue; lease liabilities (RMB6,749m) EXCLUDED from net debt; D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (~RMB1.5bn) so the lease is not charged twice. KION sale-and-leaseback / indirect-lease liabilities (long-term payables) are NOT IFRS-16 leases: they are finance-book funding and sit in debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Consolidated flows (KION ~46% owned, Shaanxi Heavy Duty Automobile 51%, others consolidated 100%); NCI charged ONCE as a bridge deduction at book value (RMB37,872m at 31-Dec-2025). NCI earned RMB2,750m in FY2025 = 7.3% on book, below the 9% cost of equity, so book is not a generous deduction. Flows are NOT reduced for the NCI profit share.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component route) + non-US/cyclical adaptations, per dcf-methods routing: Weichai is an operating industrial (engines/powertrain, Shaanxi heavy trucks, KION forklifts and supply-chain automation, Linde Hydraulics) and has no bank, REIT or holdco characteristics. Weichai has a captive forklift finance book inside KION, handled by putting all of its funding in debt and letting its income stay in the flows (see bridge note). First valuation of this ticker; no Analysis.json existed when this was built, so scenario axes come from the filings' MD&A. CASH-FLOW BASIS: PRC CAS cash flow statement puts interest paid in financing but interest received in operating, so reported FCF (OCF - cash capex) is unlevered but contains RMB3,561m of interest income; that is stripped (owner FCF 18,257) and the cash, structured deposits and time deposits that earn it go into the bridge. COMPONENT CALIBRATION: FY2025 EBIT ex finance/investment/FV items = revenue - COGS - surcharges - S&D - G&A - R&D + other income - impairments ~ RMB15.4bn; total D&A 13,598 (fixed assets/investment property/ROU 11,100 + intangibles 2,339 + LT prepaid 160), i.e. EBITDA ~12.5% of revenue. D&A (5.2% ex ROU) far exceeds cash capex (2.9%) because KION's rental/leased fleet and lease-receivable build is reinvested inside operating cash flow (the recurring RMB4-5bn 'increase in operating receivables'); capex_pct is therefore set at 4.4% = 2.9% cash capex + ~1.5% fleet/finance-book reinvestment, and wc_capture is 0 (payables+notes payable RMB104bn exceed receivables+inventory, so growth would release cash, but the fleet build consumes it; netted to zero). The calibrated FY0 build gives owner FCF after leases of ~RMB14.1bn (6.1% of revenue) vs actual FY2025 16.5bn (7.1%) and a FY2017-25 average of ~5.7% after leases (range -7% in the 2022 truck trough to 11% in 2018): base year 1 is anchored MID-CYCLE, not on FY2025. Cash tax 19% vs FY2025 book ETR 15.6% (15% high-tech rate at the parent, ~30% at KION; deferred-tax movements of RMB747m made cash tax ~20%). CYCLICAL: terminal capped at 12x FCF (Gordon at 9%/2% = 14.6x). Interim filing H1-2026 (due end-Aug 2026) is NOT in the folder; Q1-2026 (revenue +8.9%, attributable NI +13.8% y/y) is the latest extracted. Bridge uses the 31-Dec-2025 balance sheet because Q1 carries the seasonal working-capital trough (Q1-26 OCF -2.7bn; Q1-25 OCF -4.6bn reversed to +28.7bn for the year) and lacks the restricted-cash and gearing disclosures; Q1-2026 cross-check: cash + trading assets 79.5bn vs 83.5bn at YE, financial liabilities 76.7bn vs 77.0bn, pension 6.6bn vs 7.3bn, NCI 38.3bn vs 37.9bn, i.e. ~RMB4bn lower, consistent with the seasonal outflow. The FY2025 final dividend (RMB0.374 x 8,662m = 3,240m, paid mid-2026) is deducted in the bridge; the H1-2026 interim is not, because its amount is not in the folder. BUYBACKS: a funded repurchaser (RMB597m FY2024, 761.5m FY2025), so the flat count is being paid for. SBC-ZERO MARKET: SBC 0.03% of revenue; house and street coincide, band_position is not meaningful.

KION asset-securitisation financing 11,154m and loans from leasing institutions 10,691m + 4,226m current); long-term payables note V.39 (sale-and-leaseback financial liabilities 10,772m + indirect lease guarantee 748m) plus 4,317m current portion (note V.34).

net_debt_detail.finance_book_treatment: KION's forklift leasing book (lease receivables RMB25,831m = LT receivables 19,349 + current portion 6,482, plus the leased/rental fleet inside fixed assets) is funded by the securitisation, leasing-institution and sale-and-leaseback liabilities above. ALL of that funding is in total_debt; the receivables are NOT added back, because their interest and rental income is in revenue/EBITDA and their reinvestment is in the 4.4% capex path. Adding them at book as well would count the finance book twice (~RMB14bn).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: revenue 5yr CAGR 3.3% (FY2020 peak to FY2025) and 8yr CAGR 5.5% (FY2017-25), with Q1-2026 revenue +8.9% y/y
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 12.6% diverges >30% from revenue (3.3%) and EPS (1.7%) 5yr CAGRs: equity was boosted by the 2021 A-share private placement and by retained earnings at a ~12% ROE, so it overstates top-line growth and was not used. 3yr CAGRs (revenue 9.8%, EPS 30.3%) start from the FY2022 heavy-truck trough and overstate trend growth.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC - interest income: FY2020 15,914; FY2022 -11,345 (truck trough, OCF negative); FY2025 18,257. 3yr owner-FCF CAGR is not meaningful (negative base). 5yr owner-FCF CAGR 2.8% is below reported 4.9% because interest income rose from RMB1.28bn to 3.56bn on a larger cash pile, not because of SBC (immaterial).

base.narrative: FY2026 +6% (Q1 +8.9%), decelerating to 2.5%; EBITDA margin edges from 12.5% to 12.8% on large-bore/data-centre engine mix and KION's efficiency programme; owner-FCF margin ~6.1-6.3% mid-cycle.

bull.narrative: Data-centre gensets / large-bore engines and SOFC scale, HDT exports and gas trucks hold China share, KION warehouse automation recovers: 9% growth fading to 3%, EBITDA margin to 13.8%.

bear.narrative: A 2022-style China heavy-truck down-leg (-8%, -4%) plus EU tariff/industrial weakness at KION, then electric and hydrogen trucks erode diesel/gas engine content: margin troughs at 10.5% and only recovers to 11.5%; terminal growth 1.5%.

scenario_narratives.base: China heavy-duty truck volumes stay near mid-cycle (~1.0-1.1m units with exports and natural-gas trucks offsetting a soft domestic freight market), Weichai keeps its ~30%+ HDT engine share, large-bore engines for data-centre gensets and marine keep growing, and KION's efficiency programme lifts its margin modestly. Revenue +6% in FY2026 (Q1 +8.9%) fading to 2.5%; EBITDA 12.5% -> 12.8%; owner FCF ~6.1-6.3% of revenue, anchored on the FY2017-25 average rather than on the strong FY2025.
scenario_narratives.bull: The AI data-centre build-out makes large-bore engines and SOFC a material second leg, HDT exports keep growing, Weichai holds share as LNG trucks gain, and KION's supply-chain-solutions (warehouse automation) backlog converts at recovered margins. Revenue grows 9% fading to 3%, EBITDA margin reaches 13.8%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The China truck cycle turns as it did in 2022 (revenue -15% that year, OCF negative) on a weak property/infrastructure economy and pulled-forward replacement demand; KION is hit by EU/US tariff friction and weak European industrial capex; over the decade battery-electric and fuel-cell heavy trucks cut the diesel/gas engine content Weichai sells. Revenue -8% then -4%, EBITDA margin troughs at 10.5% and settles at 11.5%, terminal growth 1.5%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: Weichai is a deep cyclical whose core market fell ~50% peak-to-trough in 2022, FY2025 was an above-average cash year, and truck electrification is a structural threat to its engine franchise. Base 50% on mid-cycle anchoring. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs data-centre engines, KION's recovery and China truck share to all go right at once.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Consolidated mid-cycle owner FCF (interest income stripped, IFRS-16 lease cash charged, KION fleet reinvestment charged), discounted at a 9% CNY/EUR-blended WACC with a 12x cyclical terminal cap, bridged to the parent's equity through net financial cash (incl. all KION finance-book funding as debt), non-operating stakes, the pension deficit and minority interests at book. SBC-zero market: house and street values coincide.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cycle timing: a 2022-style China HDT downturn takes owner FCF negative for a year; the base year is mid-cycle, not trough
Minority interests deducted at book (RMB37.9bn); if KION re-rates, the NCI claim is worth more than book
KION finance-book treatment: funding in debt, receivables valued through the flows; mis-sizing the 1.5% fleet reinvestment moves value ~RMB2/share per 0.5pp
Cash quality: ~RMB28.6bn of cash sits at the related-party Shandong Heavy Industry finance company; RMB19.4bn of restricted cash/pledged deposits is excluded as working-capital collateral
Electrification of China heavy trucks eroding diesel/gas engine content
H1-2026 interim not yet in the folder; bridge is the 31-Dec-2025 balance sheet less the FY2025 final dividend
